# Results -- Study 506 (Industry-Momentum) on the real yfinance tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: Moskowitz-Grinblatt (1999)
industry momentum -- each month rank the 11 SPDR sector ETFs by their trailing **12-1** return
(skip the most recent month), go long the top winners and short the bottom losers, equal-weight,
dollar-neutral, rebalance monthly, hold one month, and **race** that book against the same machine
on a large-cap single-name survivor basket. One execution lag (form on the month-end close, earn
the next month). As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Sector ETFs (daily adjusted-close) | 5637 days x 11 ETFs | `641f8fd7befd` |
| SPY (daily adjusted-close) | 5637 days | `06ab1687a7ba` |
| Single-name basket (daily adjusted-close) | 5637 days x 40 names | `268288d86882` |
| Daily range | 2004-01-02 -- 2026-05-29 | -- |
| Monthly sector bars | 268 (2004-02 -- 2026-05) | -- |
| Sector holding months | 256 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close (`auto_adjust=True`). Universe: the 11 SPDR sectors
(XLK XLF XLE XLV XLI XLY XLP XLU XLB XLRE XLC; XLRE lists 2015-10, XLC 2018-06, so each sector
enters the rank once it has 13 months of history) plus SPY, and a fixed 40-name large-cap basket
for the single-name comparison. Costs: one-way **5 bps/leg** per rebalance + **50 bps/yr** short
borrow on the loser leg. Top/bottom **3** of 11 sectors; top/bottom **8** of 40 names.

**Survivorship bias -- named on the SIGNAL axis (not hidden in tradability):** the single-name
basket is names *still trading in 2026*. The loser leg's natural short candidates -- firms that
trended down into delisting or bankruptcy -- are absent by construction, so any single-name
momentum premium here is an **upper bound** (Shumway 1997 on the delisting bias). The sector-ETF
book is essentially **survivorship-free** (the 11 SPDR sectors are stable, index-tracking funds),
which is exactly why the industry expression is the cleaner test of Moskowitz-Grinblatt.

## Synthetic positive control (engine faithfulness -- NOT a real-tape claim)

A deterministic synthetic sector world with a planted, *persistent* (AR(1)) industry-momentum
component. The long-short must score ~0 at the null and rise monotonically as the planted
strength grows. Each row is averaged over **20 RNG seeds** (never a single lucky seed).

| Planted `industry_mom` | Long-short mean (ann) | seed-avg HAC *t* |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.00 (null) | +0.20% | **+0.18** |
| 0.06 | +41.6% | +10.50 |
| 0.12 | +83.9% | +10.84 |
| 0.20 | +139.9% | +10.93 |

At the null the seed-averaged *t* is **+0.18** -- the engine does **not** manufacture significance
from noise; with a planted component it lights up strongly and monotonically. **This is a power /
faithfulness check only; it is never cited to support the real-tape stamp.**

## The honest test -- real 12-1 momentum, industry vs single-name

One execution lag; gross long-short and net (after 5 bps/leg x turnover + 50 bps/yr borrow on the
short leg). The *t* is a Newey-West **HAC** one-sample *t* on the monthly long-short; the placebo
*p* is the share of **500 label-shuffle** nulls whose mean long-short return >= the real book's.

### Industry momentum -- 11 SPDR sector ETFs (top/bottom 3)

| Statistic | Gross | Net (costs + borrow) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean return (ann) | **+0.90%/yr** | +0.14%/yr |
| Vol (ann) | 13.83% | 13.83% |
| Sharpe (ann) | +0.065 | +0.010 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.315** | +0.048 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 53.9% | 53.1% |
| Max drawdown | -45.1% | -49.2% |
| Avg turnover/leg | 21.8%/mo | -- |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.348** | -- |

### Single-name momentum -- 40 large-cap survivors (top/bottom 8)

| Statistic | Gross | Net (costs + borrow) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean return (ann) | **+2.46%/yr** | +1.66%/yr |
| Vol (ann) | 18.73% | 18.73% |
| Sharpe (ann) | +0.131 | +0.089 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **+0.566** | +0.382 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 57.0% | 55.9% |
| Max drawdown | -59.6% | -60.1% |
| Avg turnover/leg | 25.1%/mo | -- |
| **Placebo p-value** | **0.150** | -- |

- The industry book earns **+0.90%/yr** gross at HAC *t* = **+0.315** -- statistically
  indistinguishable from zero, and the label-shuffle placebo *p* = **0.348** says the real mean is
  no better than a coin among shuffled nulls. Net of costs it collapses to **+0.14%/yr**.
- The single-name book earns **+2.46%/yr** gross at HAC *t* = **+0.566** (placebo *p* = 0.150) --
  also far below the desk's *t* >= 2 bar, and that number is the **survivorship upper bound**.
- **The race goes the wrong way.** Moskowitz-Grinblatt predict the *industry* expression carries
  the punch and subsumes single-name momentum. On this tape the single-name book is *larger*
  (+2.46%/yr vs +0.90%/yr) -- and both are noise. The industry sort does **not** beat the
  single-name sort; the headline claim does not reproduce on the modern sector-ETF tape.

## Context -- the legs are nearly tied, and beta is the story

| Sleeve | Mean (ann) |
|---|---:|
| Winner sectors (long leg) | +11.1%/yr |
| Loser sectors (short leg) | +10.2%/yr |
| SPY | +11.7%/yr |

The winner and loser sector legs earn **+11.1%** and **+10.2%** -- both essentially the market
(+11.7%). In a long-run bull tape every sector compounds, so ranking sectors on past return
separates almost nothing: the long-short is the thin **+0.9%/yr** gap between two market-like legs.

## Robustness -- sector top_k sweep (gross)

| top_k | Mean (ann) | HAC *t* | Sharpe |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | +5.00% | +0.888 | +0.201 |
| 2 | +2.48% | +0.733 | +0.144 |
| **3** | **+0.90%** | **+0.315** | +0.065 |
| 4 | -0.33% | -0.148 | -0.029 |

No cut clears *t* = 2. The single-sector (k=1) book is the largest in mean (+5.0%/yr) but on a
**one-name-per-leg** concentration its *t* is still only +0.89 -- a high-variance bet, not an edge,
and it fades monotonically as the legs widen. There is no top_k where industry momentum is real.

## Year-by-year industry long-short (gross)

| Year | LS | Year | LS | Year | LS |
|---|--:|---|--:|---|--:|
| 2005 | +6.2% | 2012 | -6.8% | 2019 | -2.8% |
| 2006 | -14.1% | 2013 | +12.2% | 2020 | +19.5% |
| 2007 | +6.7% | 2014 | -4.4% | 2021 | -15.8% |
| 2008 | +14.5% | 2015 | +9.2% | 2022 | +46.7% |
| 2009 | -16.4% | 2016 | -16.6% | 2023 | -12.1% |
| 2010 | -0.2% | 2017 | -0.5% | 2024 | -2.8% |
| 2011 | -6.7% | 2018 | -6.5% | 2025 | +3.6% |

The sign flips violently year to year (+46.7% in the 2022 energy-led selloff, -16.6% in 2016) --
the classic momentum-crash left tail with no long-run premium to compensate. The one big year
(2022) is a single sector-dispersion event, not a repeatable edge.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Industry long-short **+0.90%/yr** gross, HAC *t* = **+0.315** (placebo
  *p* = **0.348**); single-name **+2.46%/yr**, *t* = **+0.566** (*p* = 0.150). Neither clears the
  desk's *t* >= 2 bar, and survivorship -- named on the SIGNAL axis -- means the single-name number
  is already an upper bound. The synthetic control proves the engine *would* find industry momentum
  if it were there (null *t* = +0.18, monotone under a planted component); the real sector tape
  simply does not carry it. Literature support (Moskowitz-Grinblatt 1999) is strong, but per house
  rules prior alone is WEAK at most and the real tape here lands **NONE**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Best net **+1.66%/yr** (single-name) on a survivor-inflated number,
  best industry net **+0.14%/yr**, with **-45% to -60%** drawdowns and **22-25%/mo** turnover.
  Both books are inside the noise band before you even pay borrow. Nothing to trade.
- **Does industry momentum beat single-name? (3rd axis) -- BUSTED.** Moskowitz-Grinblatt's
  signature claim is that the *industry* sort carries the punch and subsumes single-name momentum.
  On the modern ETF tape the single-name book is *larger* (+2.46% vs +0.90%/yr) and both are
  indistinguishable from zero -- the industry expression does not dominate, it under-performs.
  The headline does not reproduce here.
